claims.entity: IPFS (peer-to-peer, content-addressed storage): DHT server nodes
claims.metric: share of DHT server nodes hosted in cloud data centers
claims.unit: percent of DHT server nodes (20,300 in data centers; 4,737, or 18.6 percent, non-cloud)
claims.boundary: Measurement of node IP addresses against a cloud-provider database, from DHT crawls run at least twice a day from 2023-04-18 to 2023-05-26 (101 snapshots; the Aug 2022 to Nov 2022 and Feb 2023 to Apr 2023 windows are the paper's separate DHT traffic and Hydra node collection, not these crawls) [corrected 11/04/2026 against the paper text]; counts DHT servers (nodes with a public IP address), not the machines behind NAT. Hosting location only; not energy.

source.title: The Cloud Strikes Back: Investigating the Decentralization of IPFS
source.publisher: Lancaster University eprint of the IMC 2023 paper (Balduf, Ascigil, Keizer, Pavlou, Scheuermann, Korczynski, Krol)

claims.quote: An average of 20300 (79.6%) of the nodes are hosted in data centers, with only 4737 (18.6%) non-cloud nodes.
claims.derived: The three largest providers host 13,259 nodes (51.9 percent of nodes, stated). 20,300 / (20,300 + 4,737) = 81 percent of the classified nodes, 79.6 percent of all (the paper does not state what the remainder is; it defines a BOTH label for peers with cloud and non-cloud addresses, so the remainder may be BOTH, an inference).
